Ticket Id: 195913

Dr Robins
Orthopaedic Surgeon
Head of Orthopaedic Ward
St Peter’s Hospital
Birmingham

25 October 2019

Dear Dr Robins

Re: Mr Sydney Cherry
DOB: 17/04/1947

Thank you for seeing Mr Sydney Cherry, a 73-year-old gentleman who has an exacerbation of chronic
osteoarthritis, for which he requires a surgical intervention.

Mr Cherry has had osteoarthritis since 2007 and hypertension since 2013, for which he takes Panadol
Osteo and Co-tenidone, respectively. He received multiple physiotherapy sessions to manage the knee
pain and sciatica. He is physically active, and currently lives alone.

Mr Cherry first presented on 03/03/2019 complaining of progressive bilateral knee joint pain
prodominantly in the right knee. The was tenderness along with restricted movement in the right knee.
He was consequently prescribed naproxen 250 mg twice daily.

Three weeks later, an X-ray of the right knee detected signs of severe osteoarthritis with the presence of
osteophytes and loss of joint space. Therefore, physiotherapy sessions were stated with an adjustment of     Commented [ESLDOC1]: started
the analgesia.

Despite having treatment, Mr Cherry’s condition further deteriorated. On 07/07/2019, he reported
experiencing pain at rest after walking. He was counseled on having a knee replacement, and today he
agreed.

Please note, an arthroplasty has been scheduled for the 20th of November, and Mr Cherry will be              Commented [ESLDOC2]: 20/11/2019
admitted to the hospital the day before.                                                                     (Preferred date format in the reference line and
                                                                                                             paragraphs)

It would be greatly appreciated if you could take Mr Cherry into your care. If you have any further          Commented [ESLDOC3]: Given the above, it
queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely

Doctor
